source.title: Reward expectation extinction restructures and degrades CA1 spatial maps through loss of a dopaminergic reward proximity signal.

confidence_rationale: The strongest available causal test of the exact dependency SD-024 asserts: a VTA dopaminergic signal in CA1 is what sustains reward-location over-representation, and optogenetically removing it collapses the over-representation. High source quality (Nat Commun, 2-photon calcium imaging plus circuit-specific inhibition, converging manipulations). Confidence is held below 0.9 because the paper measures over-representation as place-field COUNT/reliability in a real CA1 population, whereas SD-024 asserts a specific implementational route (extra RBF centers allocated per DA-scaled reward event) that the paper neither confirms nor excludes.
failure_signatures: When reward expectation is extinguished, over-representation of reward locations vanishes while the animal remains engaged with the environment -- so an implementation that keeps expanded density after reward removal (SD-024's 'craving' failure mode) is biologically off-pattern, not merely suboptimal.

Loss of the dopaminergic reward-proximity signal increases place-field remapping throughout the whole environment and reduces trial-to-trial reliability -- i.e. removing DA does not simply flatten the map locally, it destabilises it globally. An REE ablation that shows only a local density change may be under-modelling the mechanism.

mapping.source_claim_statement: VTA dopaminergic axons in CA1 carry a ramping reward-proximity signal that depends on reward expectation; this signal maintains place-cell over-representation of reward locations and the reliability of the surrounding map. Inhibiting VTA dopaminergic neurons largely replicates the effect of extinguishing reward expectation.
mapping.ree_translation: SD-024's core premise -- that a phasic dopaminergic signal at reward encounters is the causal driver of increased representational density at reward locations, rather than that density being a passive consequence of environmental structure or of visit frequency -- is directly supported. It also supports the SD-012 scaling choice (dopamine_signal = benefit_magnitude * drive_level): the biological signal is expectation-dependent, not merely delivery-triggered.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper's dependent variable is the distribution and reliability of place FIELDS in a recorded CA1 population. SD-024's mechanism is allocation of extra RBF centers in a fixed-capacity FIFO field, and its discriminator (compute_local_density) is deliberately weight-independent. A dopaminergic gain change on existing units would produce the paper's result without producing SD-024's; the paper therefore licenses the dependency, not the implementation. Additionally: mouse, virtual-reality linear track, head-fixed -- a far more impoverished setting than the free navigation SD-024's z_world neighbourhood is meant to abstract.
mapping.source_context: Mice, head-fixed virtual-reality linear track; 2-photon calcium imaging of CA1 place cells and of VTA dopaminergic axons in CA1; optogenetic inhibition of VTA dopaminergic neurons.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high (causal circuit manipulation with a converging behavioural manipulation). Mapping fidelity moderate: right causal arrow, wrong grain -- field statistics vs center allocation. Transfer risk moderate: rodent VR to an artificial agent's latent field, but the claim being transferred is a dependency structure rather than a parameter value.
